full_judgment: 38. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate, appeared on behalf of the respondent nos. 3,4 and 16 He submitted that all the respondent Nos. 2 to 16 strangers to the respondent-company, acted bona fide and in good-faith, in purchasing its shares for value, the receipts for which were duly granted by respondent no. 17 the Chairman, Dr. Ruhul Amin, the Managing Director and Dr. Gafoor, the Financial Director of the respondent-company. He submitted further that the respondent nos. 2 to 16 were invited by no other person than by Dr. Ruhul Amin the Managing Director himself, to the attend the meeting of the Board of Directors on 17th May, 2002, as observers and in compliance to his request they duly attended the said meeting only as observers but did not participate in the deliberations of the  meeting, as such, the allegations of threat or application of force, raised against them, was absolutely false, besides, on their appointment as directors they were all felicitated by Dr. Ruhul Amin himself, in the meeting of the Board of Directors held on 20th June, 2002, The learned Advocate further submitted that all the papers made available show that the decision to issue further. share were taken unanimously by the Board of Directors which was also duly endorsed by the company in its 14yh Annual General Meeting, that the notices to the existing share-holders were directed to be issued and some of them duly responded, that all these facts on record, raised a reasonable presumption that all the procedures required under the articles, were duly complied with and they had no way of knowing that the Managing Director did not take necessary steps to issue the required notice to the petitioner who is no less than a person that the brother of his wife. The learned Advocate highlighted in his submissions that Dr. Ruhul respondent-company starting from allotment of shares in favour of the respondents nos. 2 to 16 received the value of the shares from them, ensuring their presence in both the meeting of the Board of Directors on 17th May and 20th June, 2002, even he himself felicited them on behalf of the respondent-company on their appointment as its directors but on the other hand, he himself challenged all his own actions and steps taken on behalf of the 'respondent-company in respect of allotment of is shares in favour of the respondent nos. 2 to 16 by swearing an affidavit on 3rd April, 2003, purported to be on behalf of the respondent-company and in its interest but as matter of fact, in full and naked support of the instant petition, which apparently supplemented it. The learned Advocate submitted further that Dr. Ruhul Amin in order to maintain his control over the respondent-company and also to suppress and hide his own illegal activities, arranged to file the instant petition, using the name of his brother-in-law, through an attorney who is admittedly his own relation and an employee, unnecessarily showing himself as representing the respondent company but -without impleading him, in order to create an opportunity for him to file an affidavit-in-opposition purportedly on behalf of the respondent-company but fully and wholly supplementing the petition itself in complete derogation to the interest of the respondent-company but only to serve his own interest. The learned Advocate pointed out that when Dr. Ruhul Amin could lend one of his own employees to file the petition on behalf of the petitioner and also filed a voluminous affidavit-in-opposition, in support of the petition, instead of justifying the actions of the respondent-company and when he is so much helpful to the petitioner, it is hardly believable that he did not inform his brother-in-law, the petitioner, about the further issue of shares, The learned Advocate finally submitted that in the instant petition, Dr. Ruhul Amin is the real petitioner who engineered the filing of this petition in the name of his brother-in-law, which was signed and filed by one of his employees.
